title: Chest Pain — History Taking
description: A GP takes a full cardiac history from a 54-year-old male presenting with chest pain. Follows the SOCRATES framework.

utterances.speaker: interviewer
utterances.text: Good morning. What's brought you in today?

utterances.speaker: responder
utterances.text: I've been having this chest pain for about three days now and it's been worrying me quite a bit.

utterances.speaker: interviewer
utterances.text: I'm glad you came in. Can you point to where exactly you feel the pain?

utterances.speaker: responder
utterances.text: It's right here in the middle of my chest, sort of behind the breastbone. Sometimes it feels like it spreads a bit.

utterances.speaker: interviewer
utterances.text: When you say it spreads — where does it go?

utterances.speaker: responder
utterances.text: To my left shoulder mostly. Once or twice I thought I felt it in my jaw but I wasn't sure if that was related.

utterances.speaker: interviewer
utterances.text: That's very helpful. How would you describe the pain — is it sharp, dull, a pressure, burning?

utterances.speaker: responder
utterances.text: More of a tightness really. Like someone is squeezing my chest. It's not sharp at all.

utterances.speaker: interviewer
utterances.text: When does it tend to come on? Is there anything that triggers it?

utterances.speaker: responder
utterances.text: It's definitely worse when I'm doing something physical. Like climbing the stairs or walking fast. It started three days ago when I was mowing the lawn.

utterances.speaker: interviewer
utterances.text: And does it go away when you stop and rest?

utterances.speaker: responder
utterances.text: Yes, within a few minutes of sitting down it usually eases off. Although last night it woke me up at about 2am even though I'd been asleep for hours.

utterances.speaker: interviewer
utterances.text: That nocturnal episode is important. How severe was the pain at its worst — on a scale of 0 to 10?

utterances.speaker: responder
utterances.text: During the day maybe a 5 or 6. Last night it was probably a 7 or 8. I was quite scared.

utterances.speaker: interviewer
utterances.text: Understandably so. Have you had any other symptoms along with the chest pain — things like breathlessness, sweating, nausea, or palpitations?

utterances.speaker: responder
utterances.text: Yes, I do get breathless when the chest pain comes on. And I've noticed I've been more tired than usual this week. I don't think I've had much nausea but I did feel a bit clammy last night.

utterances.speaker: interviewer
utterances.text: Have you had anything like this before, or has this come on completely out of the blue?

utterances.speaker: responder
utterances.text: I had a mild episode maybe two years ago but the doctor at the time said it was probably indigestion and it went away. This feels different though.

utterances.speaker: interviewer
utterances.text: Do you have any history of heart problems, high blood pressure, or high cholesterol?

utterances.speaker: responder
utterances.text: I was told my blood pressure was a bit high about a year ago but I never got treatment for it. I don't know about my cholesterol.

utterances.speaker: interviewer
utterances.text: Any family history of heart disease? Parents, siblings?

utterances.speaker: responder
utterances.text: My father had a heart attack at 58. He survived but he was on a lot of medication after that.

utterances.speaker: interviewer
utterances.text: Do you smoke, or have you smoked in the past?

utterances.speaker: responder
utterances.text: I used to smoke about 15 a day but I gave up six years ago. Before that I smoked for about 20 years.

utterances.speaker: interviewer
utterances.text: Are you on any medications at the moment, prescribed or over-the-counter?

utterances.speaker: responder
utterances.text: Just some ibuprofen I've been taking for lower back pain. Nothing else regularly.

utterances.speaker: interviewer
utterances.text: Have you taken anything for the chest pain itself — like antacids or GTN spray?

utterances.speaker: responder
utterances.text: I tried some Gaviscon last night thinking it might be heartburn but it didn't help at all. No spray.
